flags.why: This is a Central Vietnamese dialect word for unfilled grain, as recorded in the [Huế dialect dictionary](https://khungcuahep.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/T%E1%BB%AB-%C4%90i%E1%BB%83n-Ph%C6%B0%C6%A1ng-Ng%E1%BB%AF-Hu%E1%BA%BF-Tr%E1%BA%A7n-Ng%E1%BB%8Dc-B%E1%BA%A3o.pdf), but it lacks a regional tag.
The example explains what an unfilled grain is instead of showing the word in ordinary use.
flags.fix: Năm ni hạn, tui sợ ló trớp hết. = There is a drought this year; I’m afraid all the rice grains will be unfilled.

flags.why: The entry omits the common conversational meaning 'off-topic; unrelated to what is being discussed,' documented in [this account of Southern usage](https://nghengu.vn/tieng-nghe-cua-toi/trot-quot-la-gi-2255.html).
flags.fix: Add: adj [Southern, colloquial] | off-topic; unrelated to what is being discussed. Example: Tui hỏi chuyện này mà ông trả lời trớt quớt. = I asked about this, but your answer was completely off-topic.

flags.why: 'Headquarters' is trụ sở, whereas trụ thạch denotes a pillar or mainstay, as explained in the [Hán–Vietnamese dictionary](https://www.hanzi.live/hanvi/tr%E1%BB%A5%20th%E1%BA%A1ch).
